description:
Discover a different side of Türkiye on an immersive journey that combines iconic cities, ancient civilizations, dramatic landscapes, and memorable railway experiences. From the historic streets of Istanbul to the remote ruins of Ani, the Black Sea mountains, the Hittite capital of Hattusa, and the cultural heart of Ankara, this itinerary goes far beyond the classic tourist route.

Your journey begins in Istanbul, exploring Ottoman heritage and the treasures of the Old Town before flying east to Kars, where Russian-era architecture and the ancient city of Ani reveal the region’s fascinating history. Travel by train through eastern Anatolia to Erzurum, continue to the lush Black Sea coast and Trabzon, and discover the spectacular Sümela Monastery.

The journey then moves inland to Divriği, home to the UNESCO-listed Great Mosque and Hospital, before boarding an overnight train toward Ankara. In Türkiye’s capital, explore Anıtkabir, the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, and the city’s Roman heritage, followed by a full day journey to Hattusa, the ancient capital of the Hittite Empire.

The adventure concludes with a high-speed train journey from Ankara back to Istanbul, bringing together Türkiye’s ancient past, diverse cultures, regional cuisines, and modern railway network in one unforgettable journey.

Highlights include: Istanbul’s Ottoman heritage, Kars and Ani, scenic eastern Anatolian train journeys, Erzurum, Trabzon and the Black Sea, Sümela Monastery, UNESCO-listed Divriği, an overnight train experience, Ankara, Hattusa and Yazılıkaya.

This is a journey designed for travelers who want to see more of Türkiye, travel more meaningfully, and experience the country beyond its most familiar destinations.

itineraries.title: Istanbul | Ottoman Heritage & Old Town
itineraries.content:
Welcome to Istanbul!

Your Türkiye by Rail journey begins at 1:00 PM with a welcome meeting with your local guide.

Begin with an orientation walk through Istanbul’s historic Old Town, taking in the atmosphere of Sultanahmet and learning about the city’s Byzantine and Ottoman heritage.

Continue to Topkapı Palace, the former imperial residence and administrative center of the Ottoman sultans for nearly four centuries. Explore its impressive courtyards, royal collections and spectacular views over the Bosphorus.

After the visit, enjoy some free time to relax or explore the surrounding historic streets before gathering for a welcome dinner featuring traditional Turkish cuisine.

Overnight: Istanbul
Meals: Welcome Dinner
Included: Local guide, Topkapı Palace entrance, orientation walk, welcome dinner

itineraries.title: Kars | Russian Heritage & Ancient Kars
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, take a domestic flight to Kars, gateway to the far east of Türkiye.

Upon arrival, begin your exploration of this fascinating border city with Kars Castle, rising above the historic center and offering panoramic views across the city. Continue to the Church of the Twelve Apostles (Kümbet Mosque), a remarkable 10th century Armenian monument that reflects the many cultural and religious layers of Kars.

Enjoy an orientation walk through the historic city center, discovering Kars's distinctive Russian-era architecture. Wide streets, basalt stone buildings and the city's planned grid reflect the period of Russian rule in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

In the evening, enjoy dinner at a local restaurant, experiencing some of the distinctive flavors of eastern Türkiye.

Overnight: Kars
Meals: Breakfast, Dinner
Included: Domestic flight, local guide, Kars Castle, Church of the Twelve Apostles, city orientation walk

itineraries.title: Kars & Ani | The Lost City of Ani
itineraries.content:
Today’s highlight is a journey to the ancient ruins of Ani, one of Türkiye’s most remarkable archaeological sites and once a thriving medieval capital on the Silk Road.

After breakfast, travel from Kars to Ani, passing through the dramatic landscapes of eastern Türkiye. Explore the atmospheric ruins with your guide, including the Cathedral of Ani, Church of St. Gregory, Church of the Redeemer and the ancient city walls.

Walk among the remains of this once-great city, situated dramatically on the edge of a gorge overlooking the border with Armenia. Your guide will bring Ani’s Armenian, Byzantine, Seljuk and Silk Road history to life.

After exploring Ani, return to Kars and enjoy the remainder of the afternoon at leisure. Take time to relax, revisit the city center or discover more of Kars’s distinctive local character.

Overnight: Kars
Meals: Breakfast, Dinner
Included: Private transportation to Ani, local guide, Ani archaeological site entrance, guided exploration of Ani

itineraries.title: Kars to Erzurum by Train
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, we board the morning train from Kars to Erzurum, beginning another scenic chapter of our Türkiye by Rail journey.

Train journey: 8:00 AM – 12:00 PM

Sit back and enjoy the changing landscapes of eastern Türkiye as the train travels through the dramatic highlands and mountains of the region.

Upon arrival in Erzurum, meet your local guide and begin exploring this historic city, once an important stop along the ancient Silk Road.

Visit the Çifte Minareli Medrese, one of Erzurum’s most impressive Seljuk monuments, before taking an orientation walk through Erzurum’s historic streets.

In the evening, enjoy a special traditional dinner in one of Erzurum’s historic houses, experiencing authentic local cuisine and the warm hospitality of eastern Türkiye.

Overnight: Erzurum
Meals: Breakfast, Dinner
Included: Train journey Kars–Erzurum, local guide, Çifte Minareli Medrese, city orientation walk, traditional Erzurum house dinner

itineraries.title: Erzurum to Trabzon | From the Highlands to the Black Sea
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, leave Erzurum and travel towards Trabzon, descending from the highlands towards the lush landscapes of Türkiye’s Black Sea coast.

Upon arrival, begin your exploration of Trabzon with a visit to the historic Hagia Sophia, a remarkable Byzantine monument reflecting the city’s long history between the Black Sea, Byzantium and the Ottoman Empire. Continue to Atatürk Mansion, surrounded by gardens and overlooking the city.

Later, explore Trabzon’s lively historic center with an orientation walk through Meydan, Uzun Sokak and the traditional bazaar streets.

End the afternoon at Boztepe, one of the city’s best viewpoints, where you can enjoy panoramic views across Trabzon and the Black Sea.

In the evening, enjoy a relaxed dinner featuring Black Sea cuisine, with local specialties such as kuymak, fresh fish or Akçaabat köfte.

Overnight: Trabzon
Meals: Breakfast, Dinner
Included: Transportation Erzurum–Trabzon, local guide, Hagia Sophia, Atatürk Mansion, city orientation walk, Boztepe

itineraries.title: Trabzon | Sümela Monastery & Black Sea Culture
itineraries.content:
Today we leave the city behind and travel into the spectacular mountains surrounding Trabzon.

Our highlight is Sümela Monastery, dramatically built into the cliffs of Altındere Valley. Explore the monastery, its chapels, rock church and historic frescoes while enjoying the spectacular forested landscape of the national park.

Continue through the Maçka Valley, stopping in Hamsiköy, a traditional mountain village famous for its local cuisine and particularly its celebrated rice pudding.

Return to Trabzon in the afternoon with time to relax or explore the city independently.

In the evening, enjoy a local Black Sea dinner, completing your two days in Trabzon with the flavors and hospitality of the region.

Overnight: Trabzon
Meals: Breakfast, Dinner
Included: Private transportation, local guide, Sümela Monastery, Altındere Valley, Maçka Valley, Hamsiköy visit

itineraries.title: Trabzon to Divriği | UNESCO Heritage & Overnight Train
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, leave Trabzon and travel towards Divriği, a historic town known for one of Türkiye’s greatest masterpieces of medieval Islamic architecture.

The highlight of the day is a visit to the Divriği Great Mosque and Hospital (Divriği Ulu Camii ve Darüşşifası), a spectacular 13th-century monument celebrated for its extraordinary stone carvings and architectural detail. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important examples of Seljuk-era architecture in Türkiye.

After exploring Divriği and its historic surroundings, enjoy some time to relax before continuing to the railway station.

In the evening, board the 7:49 PM overnight train to Ankara. Settle into your cabin and experience one of the most memorable parts of your Türkiye by Rail journey — travelling through the heart of Anatolia overnight by train.

Overnight: Overnight train to Ankara
Meals: Breakfast
Included: Private Transportation Trabzon–Divriği, Divriği Ulu Camii and Darüşşifası visit, train to Ankara

itineraries.title: Ankara | The Heart of Modern Türkiye
itineraries.content:
Arrive in Ankara at approximately 10:30 AM after your overnight train journey. Meet your local guide and begin exploring Türkiye’s capital.

Start with Anıtkabir, the monumental mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and one of the most important symbols of modern Türkiye.

After the visit, continue to your hotel for check-in and some time to refresh.

In the afternoon, visit the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, home to an exceptional collection tracing thousands of years of Anatolian history, including the remarkable heritage of the Hittites.

Continue with a walk through Ankara’s ancient past, visiting the Temple of Augustus, an important Roman monument, followed by the Roman Baths of Ankara, where you can see the remains of the city's Roman-era public life.

After a full day exploring Ankara from its ancient civilizations to the foundation of the modern Turkish Republic, enjoy the evening at leisure.

Overnight: Ankara
Meals: Breakfast
Included: Local guide, Anıtkabir, Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, Temple of Augustus, Roman Baths

itineraries.title: Hattusa | Journey into the Hittite World
itineraries.content:
Today, leave Ankara after breakfast for a full-day journey to Hattusa, the ancient capital of the Hittite Empire and one of Türkiye’s most important archaeological sites.

Explore the monumental ruins of Hattusa, including the Great Temple, Lion Gate, Royal Gate, ancient city walls, and the remains of the royal quarter. Your local guide will bring the Hittite civilization to life as you discover the history of this powerful Bronze Age empire.

Continue to Yazılıkaya, a remarkable open-air rock sanctuary just outside Hattusa, where impressive reliefs depict Hittite gods and religious ceremonies.

After the visit, enjoy lunch featuring local Çorum cuisine before returning to Ankara in the afternoon. The evening is free to relax or explore Ankara at your own pace.

Overnight: Ankara
Meals: Breakfast
Included: Private transportation, local guide, Hattusa entrance, Yazılıkaya entrance, guided archaeological visit, local lunch.

itineraries.title: Ankara to Istanbul by High-Speed Train
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, board the high speed train from Ankara to Istanbul and enjoy a comfortable journey through the landscapes of central Türkiye.

Upon arrival in Istanbul, your Türkiye by Rail journey comes to an end at the Istanbul train station. From here, you can continue to your hotel, airport, or onward journey independently.

Meals: Breakfast
Included: High speed train ticket from Ankara to Istanbul

title.rendered: Sunrise Walking Tour of Istanbul With Traditional Breakfast

description:
Experience Istanbul before the city wakes up on our Sunrise Walking Tour, a peaceful and unforgettable way to discover the historic heart of the city.

Start your morning in Sultanahmet, where the streets and squares are beautifully quiet at sunrise. Walk through the historic Hippodrome and admire the magnificent Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia in the soft morning light. Continue through the atmospheric streets of the Old City, discovering Istanbul’s fascinating history while avoiding the crowds of the later hours.

After your morning walk, cross to the Asian side of Istanbul by local ferry and enjoy the city from the water as the Bosphorus comes alive. Finish your experience with a traditional Turkish breakfast, featuring fresh bread, cheeses, olives, eggs, tomatoes, cucumbers, jams, honey, and Turkish tea.

This experience combines history, local life, the Bosphorus, and authentic Turkish cuisine—all in one beautiful morning.

itineraries.title: Red & Rose Valley Hike ( 10 - 12 km )
itineraries.content:
Enjoy a scenic hike through Cappadocia’s beautiful Red and Rose Valleys, famous for their colorful rock formations, fairy chimneys, cave churches, and peaceful vineyard trails. Walk along winding paths and narrow canyon passages while discovering hidden chapels carved into the cliffs.

Take a relaxing break at a local valley café before continuing toward the panoramic viewpoints of Red Valley, where the landscape glows with stunning shades of red and pink, especially at sunset.

Hiking Distance: Approx. 10–12 km

Accommodation : Tas Konak Cave Hotel or Similar

itineraries.title: Love Valley Hike ( 8 - 10 km )
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, set out for a scenic nature trek through the beautiful Love Valley, famous for its towering fairy chimneys and unique volcanic rock formations. Walk along peaceful trails surrounded by vineyards, orchards, and dramatic canyon scenery while enjoying spectacular views of Cappadocia’s landscape.

Continue toward Uçhisar, the highest point in Cappadocia, passing through quiet village paths and natural valleys along the way. Enjoy panoramic views of the region and explore the charming atmosphere of Uçhisar Village beneath its impressive rock castle.

This easy to moderate hike offers a perfect combination of nature, local life, and breathtaking scenery.

Hiking Distance : Approx. 8–10 km

Accommodation : Ciner Hotel or Similar

itineraries.title: Ihlara Valley Nature & River Hike ( 12 - 14 km )
itineraries.content:
Drive to the stunning Ihlara Valley, one of Cappadocia’s most beautiful canyon landscapes. Enjoy a scenic trek along the Melendiz River surrounded by lush greenery, towering cliffs, and peaceful nature far from the crowds.

Walk through the canyon while discovering ancient rock-cut churches, hidden cave dwellings, and frescoed chapels carved into the valley walls by early Christian communities centuries ago. Along the route, enjoy relaxing riverside breaks at local cafés set beside the flowing river.

This refreshing hike combines nature, history, and local atmosphere, offering a completely different side of Cappadocia.

Hiking Distance: Approx. 12–14 km

Accommodation : Ciner Hotel or Similar

itineraries.title: Pigeon Valley Hike ( 6 - 8 km )
itineraries.content:
Continue with a scenic hike through Pigeon Valley, famous for its panoramic views, cave dwellings, and traditional pigeon houses carved into the cliffs. Walk along peaceful valley trails surrounded by unique rock formations and beautiful Cappadocian landscapes stretching between Uçhisar and Göreme.

This experience offers a perfect blend of Cappadocia’s rich history, local culture, and stunning natural scenery.

Hiking Distance: Approx. 6–8 km

Accommodation : Ciner Hotel or Similar

itineraries.title: Ortahisar Hidden Valley Hike ( 7 - 9 km )
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, explore the authentic village atmosphere of Ortahisar, one of Cappadocia’s most traditional and less-visited towns. Walk through quiet stone streets, local neighborhoods, and scenic countryside paths beneath the impressive Ortahisar Rock Castle.

Continue with a peaceful hike through hidden valleys away from the crowds, surrounded by dramatic rock formations, cave dwellings, orchards, and small local farms. Along the way, enjoy beautiful panoramic viewpoints and experience the untouched side of Cappadocia’s natural landscape.

This easy to moderate hike offers a perfect combination of local culture, nature, and off-the-beaten-path discovery. Hiking Distance: Approx. 7–9 km.

Hiking Distance: Approx. 7–9 km

itineraries.title: Departure
itineraries.content:
Early this morning, enjoy an unforgettable Sunrise hot air balloon ride over Cappadocia’s magical landscape. Drift above fairy chimneys, colorful valleys, rock formations, and cave villages while watching the sunrise illuminate the region in stunning shades of gold and pink.

After the flight, celebrate with a traditional certificate and light refreshment before returning to your hotel for breakfast and check-out.

Depending on your flight time, enjoy some free time for last-minute shopping, relaxing at a local café.

Enjoy s soak in the warm, mineral-rich waters of the thermal pools, taking in the breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape. Along the way, we’ll enjoy a taste of delicious Turkish ice cream before continuing to discover the remains of the Old Seljuk civilization settlements. After the guided visits, you will have some free time to wander through the charming streets and enjoy shopping at your own pace.

We then continue to the elegant Karatay Tile Museum, where you will admire exquisite examples of 13th-century Seljuk tile art and craftsmanship, reflecting the artistic brilliance of the Seljuk era.

In the evening, enjoy a delicious dinner featuring authentic Central Anatolian cuisine at one of Konya’s well-known traditional restaurants and a perfect opportunity to savor the local flavors and unwind after a culturally enriching day.

Overnight in Konya

Wander through the charming alleys of the old bazaar area, including Bakırcılar Çarşısı (Coppersmith Bazaar), where you can watch artisans at work and shop for handcrafted souvenirs. For dinner, indulge in Gaziantep’s legendary cuisine at İmam Çağdaş, one of the most famous kebab restaurants in the country. Share a traditional meal, learn about their culture, and discover the stories behind their special dishes. description:
Explore Kaş: Nature, History, and the Sea – A Perfect Mediterranean Escape

Nestled along the stunning turquoise coast of Turkey, Kaş offers the perfect mix of adventure, culture, and relaxation. Start your journey with trade two wheels for a paddle and head out on a kayaking adventure over the sunken city of Kekova. Glide across crystal-clear waters as you pass over ancient ruins submerged just beneath the surface, and stop by the charming village of Kaleköy (Simena), only accessible by boat or foot. It’s a peaceful, unforgettable way to connect with the region’s deep history. Bike ride through the scenic hills and coastline, where olive groves, ancient ruins, and panoramic sea views await at every turn. Whether you're cycling through peaceful villages or challenging yourself on mountain paths, it's a refreshing way to experience the natural beauty of the region. For a journey even further back in time, visit the ancient Lycian sites of Letoon and Xanthos. These UNESCO World Heritage Sites are home to stunning temple ruins, grand theaters, and mysterious inscriptions. Walking among the stones, you’ll feel the echoes of civilizations that flourished thousands of years ago. To cool off, head inland to Saklıkent Gorge, one of the deepest canyons in Turkey. Walk through the icy mountain stream, splash through narrow passages carved by centuries of water, or just relax in one of the riverside cafes with your feet in the water. It’s the perfect spot to recharge and escape the summer heat.

Cap off your Kaş adventure with a full-day boat trip along the coast. Sail to hidden bays, swim in secluded coves, and snorkel above vibrant underwater life. Enjoy a freshly prepared Turkish lunch onboard, bask in the sun, and let the rhythm of the waves carry your worries away. It’s the ultimate blend of leisure and exploration.

itineraries.title: Welcome to İzmir (Smyrna)
itineraries.content:
Upon arrival, transfer to your hotel and enjoy some time to settle in. At 1:00 PM, meet your guide for a welcome briefing before beginning your exploration of this vibrant Aegean city.

Start your journey with a visit to the ancient Agora of Smyrna, once the bustling heart of Roman-era trade and daily life. Continue to Kadifekale (Velvet Castle), where you’ll be rewarded with panoramic views over the city and the Gulf of İzmir. Then visit the historic Church of Saint Polycarp, one of the oldest churches in the city, rich in history and religious significance.

In the evening, enjoy a relaxing dinner along the lively Kordon Waterfront, famous for its seaside promenade, cafés, and beautiful sunset views.

Accommodation: Pier Passport Hotel or similar

itineraries.title: Pergamum Discovery – Ancient Wonders of the North Aegean
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, enjoy a scenic drive (approx. 2 hours) to Bergama, the site of the ancient city of Pergamum, one of the most powerful cultural centers of the Hellenistic world.
Explore the magnificent Pergamon Acropolis, dramatically perched on a hilltop overlooking the valley below. Here, you will visit the impressive Theater of Pergamon, one of the steepest ancient theaters in the world, and the remains of the Temple of Zeus at Pergamon, once a grand sanctuary dedicated to the king of the gods.
Continue to the remarkable Red Basilica, a massive Roman temple complex later converted into a Christian basilica, showcasing layers of religious history.
After your visit, you may choose to stay overnight in Bergama for a more relaxed experience, or return to İzmir.
Accommodation: Pier Passport Hotel or similar

itineraries.title: Thyatira & Sardis – Tracing Ancient Civilizations
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, depart for Thyatira (approx. 1.5 hours), one of the ancient cities mentioned in the Book of Revelation. Explore the remains of the basilica and visit the small local museum, offering insight into the city's early Christian heritage.
Continue your journey to Sardis (approx. 1 hour), once the capital of the ancient Lydian Kingdom and home of the legendary King Croesus. Here, you will visit the impressive Temple of Artemis at Sardis, the grand Sardis Gymnasium, and the beautifully restored Ancient Synagogue of Sardis, one of the largest synagogues of the ancient world.
After the tour, continue to your hotel for an overnight stay in Salihli or Alaşehir.
Accommodation: Can Deluxe Hotel or similar

itineraries.title: Philadelphia & Laodicea – Echoes of Early Christianity
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, visit Philadelphia, one of the Seven Churches of Revelation. Explore the remains of a Byzantine-era church and sections of the ancient fortress walls, offering a glimpse into the city’s enduring spiritual heritage.

Continue your journey to Laodicea (approx. 2 hours), an important ancient city known for its wealth and significance in early Christianity. Discover its impressive ruins, including ancient theaters, agoras, and remarkably preserved early Christian structures.

After the tour, drive to Pamukkale, famous for its stunning white travertine terraces and thermal waters.

Overnight in Pamukkale, near the hot springs.

Accommodation: Venus Boutique Hotel or similar

itineraries.title: Pamukkale & Ephesus – Natural Wonders and Ancient Glory
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, visit the breathtaking Pamukkale Travertines, a natural wonder of cascading white terraces formed by mineral-rich thermal waters. You may also choose to explore the nearby Hierapolis (optional but highly recommended), an ancient spa city featuring impressive ruins including a grand theater, necropolis, and the famous Antique Pool.
Following your visit, enjoy a scenic drive (approx. 2 hours) to Ephesus, one of the best-preserved ancient cities in the Mediterranean.
Overnight in Selçuk.
Accommodation: Kalehan Boutique Hotel or similar

itineraries.title: Ephesus – A Journey Through Ancient Splendor
itineraries.content:
After breakfast, explore the magnificent ancient city of Ephesus, one of the best-preserved classical cities in the world. Walk along its marble streets and discover iconic landmarks such as the stunning Library of Celsus and the impressive Grand Theater of Ephesus, once capable of holding thousands of spectators.
Continue to the remains of the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. You may also choose to visit the sacred House of the Virgin Mary or the historic Basilica of St. John, both important pilgrimage sites with deep religious significance.
After your visit, enjoy a comfortable drive back to İzmir (approx. 1 hour).
Overnight in İzmir.
Accommodation: Pier Passport Hotel or similar

faqs.title: Do I need a visa to visit Türkiye ?
faqs.content: Visa requirements may change and depends on Nationality. Please check the Turkish embassy website in your country of departure.

faqs.title: What vaccinations are required for Turkey ?
faqs.content: Recommended vaccinations include hepatitis a, hepatitis b, rabies, and tetanus. For more details, please check WHO official website.

faqs.title: When’s the best time to visit Eastern Turkey?
faqs.content: Best time to visit between 1st of May to 30th of September.

faqs.title: What’s the weather like in Eastern Turkey?
faqs.content: April- May and September - October is colder than June , July , August. The hottest month of the year is July, with an average daily maximum of 25°C. North east is cold, south east is very hot.

faqs.title: Are there ATMs widely popular and are credit cards accepted widely ?
faqs.content: Yes, ATMs are widely available in large cities and towns, and both Visa and Mastercard are widely accepted. Credit Card Accepted almost in all businesses.

faqs.title: What about internet access?
faqs.content: Yes. The Internet can be accessed in most places. Sometimes, there might be some technical problems. The Internet in Türkiye is not as fast as you are used to and at times you can just lose connection.

faqs.title: Is there tipping in Türkiye ?
faqs.content: it is customary in Türkiye to tip service providers such as waiters, at approximately 10%, depending on the service.  Tipping is expected, though not compulsory, and shows an expression of satisfaction with the people helping you on your tour. Recommendations for tipping Tour Leader / Guide is Per Person Per Day 10 usd, For Your Driver 5 usd per person per day, depending on the quality of the service.

faqs.title: Is the tap water in Turkey safe to drink?
faqs.content: it’s often heavily chlorinated, so you may choose to drink bottled water instead.

faqs.title: Is Turkey safe?
faqs.content:
Turkey is a very safe country in which to visit — particularly within tourist areas.

However, that said, it always pays to be aware of petty crime (like pickpocketing), tourist scams, and touts — particularly in larger cities. It’s uncommon, but female travellers might also attract some unwarranted attention. Dress modestly and you should be fine.

faqs.title: Do I need a Visa For Turkiye ?
faqs.content:
Travellers from most European Union countries and some South American and Asian countries can travel to Turkey without a visa for up to 90 days within a 180-day period. All other nationals will need to apply for a visa online (e-visa) or through a Turkish embassy or consulate before traveling.

Visas are the responsibility of the individual traveller. Entry requirements can change at any time, so it's important that you check for the latest information.

You can check the entry requirements for your nationality on your government's foreign travel advisories, the Republic of Turkey's website or our visa and entry requirements page.

faqs.title: Is tipping customary in Turkiye ?
faqs.content:
It’s normal to tip 10 to 15% of the bill in cafes, restaurants and bars in Turkey (if the bill doesn’t include gratuity already). Hotel and hamam (Turkish bathhouse) staff may also expect a small tip. Tipping taxi drivers is unnecessary, although rounding up the fare for convenience is common.

Recommendation for your Tour Leader is 10 usd Per Person Per day, For Driver 5 usd per person per day.

faqs.title: Is Tap water drinkable in Türkiye ?
faqs.content: Drinking tap water isn't recommended in Turkey. For environmental reasons, try to avoid buying bottled water. Fill a reusable water bottle or canteen with filtered water or carry water purification tablets with you.

faqs.title: What is internet access in Türkiye ?
faqs.content: There are many free wi-fi spots in Turkey’s cities, and most restaurants, cafes and bars offer wi-fi to customers. You can use freely. internet speed might be slower in public places.

faqs.title: Is Turkiye safe for LGBTQIA+ travellers ?
faqs.content:
Turkey is generally a safe destination for LGBTQIA+ travellers but Türkiye is a predominantly Muslim country, and societal attitudes toward LGBTQIA+ individuals can be conservative, especially in rural areas. Larger cities like Istanbul, Ankara, and Izmir tend to have more LGBTQIA+-friendly spaces, including bars, clubs, and organizations.

Public displays of affection, regardless of orientation, may attract unwanted attention in more conservative areas.

Risks and Challenges

  • Pride Events: Pride parades and other LGBTQIA+ events have faced restrictions or bans in recent years, often accompanied by police crackdowns.
  • Public Behavior: Openly expressing LGBTQIA+ identities or affection in public could lead to harassment or discrimination in certain areas.
  • Safety Concerns: While violence against LGBTQIA+ travelers is not common, being discreet and situationally aware is advisable.

Practical Tips for LGBTQIA+ Travelers

  1. Stay in LGBTQIA+-Friendly Neighborhoods: Areas like Beyoğlu in Istanbul are known for their more progressive attitudes and LGBTQIA+ venues.
  2. Use Apps for Recommendations: Platforms like Spartacus or GeoSure can provide insights on LGBTQIA+-friendly locations and safety ratings.
  3. Be Cautious Online: If using dating apps, meet in public places and verify the identity of individuals to avoid scams or entrapment.
  4. Dress and Act Accordingly: While being yourself is important, being mindful of local norms can help avoid unwanted attention.
  5. Research Local LGBTQIA+ Organizations: Groups like Kaos GL and SPoD can offer support or advice.

In Summary

Türkiye can be a rewarding destination for LGBTQIA+ travelers, but it’s important to be aware of the local cultural and social climate. Larger cities are generally more welcoming, while discretion is advised in conservative or rural areas. By taking precautions and planning carefully, you can enjoy a safe and enriching visit.

Visit the world-renowned Zeugma Mosaic Museum, home to some of the most stunning Roman mosaics ever discovered, including the iconic “Gypsy Girl.” This museum offers a fascinating glimpse into the region’s ancient past. Wander through the charming alleys of the old bazaar area, including Bakırcılar Çarşısı (Coppersmith Bazaar), where you can watch artisans at work and shop for handcrafted souvenirs. For dinner, indulge in Gaziantep’s legendary cuisine at İmam Çağdaş, one of the most famous kebab restaurants in the country. Try local specialties such as Ali Nazik kebab, lamb skewers, and freshly baked lahmacun.

Share a traditional meal, learn about their culture, and discover the stories behind their special dishes. Afterward, we drive to Mount Nemrut to see the giant stone heads and Watch the sun set over the colossal statues of this UNESCO World Heritage Site at 2,000 m.

Today you will try Urfa Kebab – The iconic local kebab made from seasoned minced meat grilled over charcoal. Less spicy than some other regional kebabs but deeply flavorful. Enjoy your meal.
